17. Social Choice and Welfare

Arrow's impossibility theorem and social welfare functions — the trade-offs of preference aggregation and inequality aversion.

  • Arrow's Theorem — Switch preference profiles and aggregation rules. On the Condorcet profile majority rule cycles; under Borda, removing an irrelevant alternative flips the ranking (IIA violation). No rule satisfies all four conditions.
  • Social Welfare Functions — Maximize CES social welfare over the utility possibility set. Sliding ρ\rhoρ from 1 to −∞-\infty−∞ moves the optimum from the utilitarian point (9.22,6.40)(9.22, 6.40)(9.22,6.40) to the Rawls point (7.68,7.68)(7.68, 7.68)(7.68,7.68).
